items.title: Dollar General Stock Rises After Earnings. The Gains Are About More Than Low Expectations.
items.summary: Dollar General  stock jumped Thursday after the discount retailer’s quarterly earnings surpassed Wall Street expectations and the company raised its guidance.  The results, which included encouraging traffic trends, were a relief after the shares’ recent underperformance.  The company reported earnings of $2.48 a share in the fiscal second quarter ended July 31, up from $1.86 a year ago and above Wall Street estimates of $2.01.

items.title: Build-A-Bear Cuts Revenue View, Fires Exec After Summer Line Flop
items.summary: The retailer cut its outlook for the second time this year and fired its chief growth officer after logging disappointing revenue and traffic in the second quarter.

items.title: Dollar Tree Earnings Score With Tariff Refunds. Why the Stock Is Falling.
items.summary: Shares of  Dollar Tree  declined Thursday as disappointing quarterly guidance overshadowed the discount retailer’s big win from tariff refunds that boosted earnings.  The company posted adjusted earnings of $2.70 a share in its fiscal second quarter ended Aug. 1, up from 77 cents a year ago and well above Wall Street expectations for $1.15.  Dollar Tree  said quarterly earnings included a benefit of $1.31 a share from tariff refunds.
